hypothesis: Per-chunk action diffusion timesteps improve paired val40 action loss by at least 0.25 percentage points beyond the quantile single-timestep E24 arm while preserving positive video improvement.
single_variable: Sample eight independent action noise timesteps per training window, one for each four-action chunk, instead of one timestep shared by all 32 actions. Quantile normalization, initialization, seed, windows, architecture and optimizer remain fixed.
parent_baseline: E24 quantile single-timestep s100: val40 action improvement 0.676% and video improvement 2.165% from the same quantile initialization.

references.title: Causal World Modeling for Robot Control

architecture.upstream_code: LingBot four streams share Wan blocks
architecture.local: four streams share H3 blocks, tail-2 trainable
architecture.rationale: Backbone port is fixed across E24/E25.

data.local: same first 800 v7 windows as E24

action.upstream_code: four actions per latent frame; q01/q99
action.local: four actions per causal chunk; q01/q99
action.rationale: H3 VAE geometry prevents an exact Wan latent-frame reshape, so shared causal chunk identity is used.

objective.upstream_code: LingBot samples a timestep for every action frame; MiniWorld samples non-decreasing chunk timesteps
objective.local: one independent shifted timestep per four-action chunk
objective.rationale: This removes the shared-window timestep shortcut while respecting H3's eight action chunks.

optimization.rationale: Mechanism evidence is required before scale.

evaluation.local: paired val40, then causal sample40 only if threshold passes
evaluation.rationale: A cheap leak-free gate prevents repeated zero-success rollouts.

evidence: fixed LingBot commit and local MiniWorld checkout
per-chunk time embedding and final norm implemented

decision.rationale: Train s100 and compare to the same quantile initialization. Run causal sample40 only if action improvement reaches at least 0.926% and video improvement remains positive; otherwise stop without rollout.
